title: Probe Consolidator: lightweight aggregators for tenant-aware inference KPIs
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background:
Redwood collects a mix of Prometheus-native metrics and OTLP spans/metrics from inference nodes, SDKs, and gateways. As usage grows we are hitting two problems: (1) high-cardinality spikes from customer-specific labels and dynamic prompt metadata that blow up Prometheus series counts, and (2) cross-source correlation gaps between OTLP traces and Prometheus time series (exemplars/trace links) for per-request latency/error attribution.

Goal:
Ship a "Probe Consolidator" (pcd) component that runs as a lightweight aggregator (sidecar or daemonset) colocated with inference frontends. The pcd will:
- perform early label sanitization and tenant-aware rollups to keep cardinality bounded,
- emit stable Prometheus-friendly series and OTLP metrics with exemplar pointers to traces,
- provide adaptive sampling rules and delta-rollups for high-volume routes (batching/burst-aware),
- expose a compact control plane endpoint for rollout and dynamic policy changes.

Non-goals:
- This work is not a full replacement for long-term analytics; it focuses on short-term SLO telemetry and alerting metrics.
- We will not change existing user-facing SDKs in this ticket except for a minimal opt-in probe header.

Design summary (high-level):
1) Ingestion: pcd receives raw OTLP/Prom push traffic from local inference processes and SDK sidecars.
2) Normalization: label whitelist/blacklist, optional redaction of prompt-derived metadata, and cardinality tokenization (hashing of high-cardinality keys with per-tenant salt).
3) Rollup Sieve: apply per-tenant/route policies: exact, low-cardinality, or hashed buckets.
4) Exemplar Linking: attach trace_id exemplars to representative histogram buckets and emit OTLP exemplar pointers for later trace lookup.
5) Export: forward stable Prometheus metrics to pushgateway or remote_write and OTLP to telemetry-gateway with backpressure/resilience.

Key implementation decisions and trade-offs:
- Where to run pcd: sidecar provides maximum fidelity but increases per-pod resource costs. We will start with a daemonset/shared pcd per node with route-aware tagging; product teams can opt into sidecar mode for critical tenants.
- Cardinality strategy: prefer deterministic hashed buckets over aggressive label dropping to preserve separation between heavy tenants. Bucketing config will be per-tenant and changeable via control plane.
- Exemplars: storing exemplars increases storage/ingester cost; we will sample exemplars at route-level budgets (default 0.05% of requests) and allow bumping for P0 customers.

Data flow and components (names):
- Probe Consolidator (pcd) daemonset: ingest -> normalize -> rollup -> export.
- Rollup Sieve: policy engine (config-driven).
- Exemplar Linker v2: deterministic exemplar sampler with backpressure integration.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow delivering stable low-cardinality Prometheus metrics for a synthetic 1M req/day tenant without >10x series explosion.
- Exemplars present and traceable for >95% of sampled exemplar events in Grafana traces.
- No >5% increase in p50/p95 request latency for colocated inference processes when pcd is enabled.
- Config-driven per-tenant rollups applied successfully via control-plane API.

Testing and validation plan:
- Load test harness generating multi-tenant traffic (see repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observe-load-harness, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observe-load-harness/pull/12).
- Staging dashboard: Grafana dashboard copy at https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-probe/pcd-staging (temp).
- Canary rollout: enable pcd for a single non-critical tenant, monitor series cardinality and SLOs for 48 hours, then expand.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha (week 1): daemonset pcd in staging; smoke tests.
- Beta (week 2): enable for 3 internal tenants; measure resource profiles and cardinality.
- Canary (week 3): enable for 10% traffic of selected customer; retention metrics and exemplar integrity checks.
- GA (week 6): opt-in configuration available to all dedicated/private customers; default for new nodes in hosted.

Progress updates and review notes:
- 2026-03-02 (Aisha): RFC posted on Confluence and shared with infra/telemetry teams: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Probe+Consolidator+RFC. Requesting feedback on cardinality model.
- 2026-03-04 (Diego): Initial prototype: daemonset ingest + whitelist normalization implemented in branch https://github.com/redwood-inference/pcd/tree/feature/normalize. Benchmark shows 4% CPU increase on smallest node type.
- 2026-03-06 (SRE review): Concern about OTLP backpressure when remotes are flaky. Action: add bounded queue with drop-and-metric counter + retry jitter (DONE).
- 2026-03-09 (PM review - Lina): Requested explicit per-tenant controls and default conservative exemplar budget. Added control plane API v0 at /pcd/v1/config (proto in repo).
- 2026-03-11 (Security): Requested threat model and proof that prompt redaction cannot leak PII. Working on design doc addendum; initial reviewer notes attached in Confluence.
- 2026-03-12 (QA): Load test run completed for 200k req/hour: series growth limited to 2.1x baseline vs 12x previously; exemplar linkage success 98% for sampled set. Artifacts: https://storage.redwood.ai/pcd/loadtest/2026-03-12-report.pdf
- 2026-03-13 (Diego): Preparing PR for normalization and rollup-sieve: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pcd/pull/34 (WIP).

Open items / risks:
- Long-term query cost implications for hashed-bucket approach vs aggressive dropping. Need product decision on retention vs fidelity for non-critical customers.
- Edge-case of third-party SDKs emitting unknown labels; currently blocked by SDK signal but we will add a per-tenant denylist fallback.
- Security sign-off pending; timeline may slip if additional redaction controls required.

Related tickets and artifacts:
- ENG-81299 (collector-sidecar-schema-adaptor) - dependency for schema compatibility utilities.
- ENG-642910 (kpi-edge-buffering-and-delta-telemetry) - dependency for buffering/backpressure behavior.
- Confluence RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Probe+Consolidator+RFC
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pcd/tree/feature/normalize
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-probe/pcd-staging

Next steps (short):
- Finalize PR for normalization + rollup-sieve (target 2026-03-15).
- Add control-plane auth to /pcd/v1/config and schedule security tabletop (2026-03-17).
- Prepare canary run plan and alerting thresholds (2026-03-20).

Owners: Diego (implementation), Aisha (spec + product coordination), SRE: Marcus Li (operational runbook).

Operational runbook snippets (where to look):
- Restart pcd: kubectl rollout restart ds/pcd -n inference-observability
- Check queue/drop counters: kubectl port-forward svc/pcd-metrics 9091:9091 && curl http://localhost:9091/metrics | grep pcd_queue_drops

Notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to the metric ingestion/aggregation surface; downstream long-term analytics and billing alignment will be separate work (follow-up ticket to be created after GA).
